A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 61 readable pages including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 3–61 are identical; differences on pages 1–2 are editorial and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original image-generation experiments, FID comparisons, memorization measurements, numerical simulations, and training-cost measurements.

after.justification: Retains the original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix B, including generation quality, memorization, sampling behavior, and computational costs.

M1.justification: Noise Unconditioning, Temperature Smoothing, their training objectives, KNN approximations, and sampling procedures are unchanged in Sections 2–5 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Cat-Caracal, CIFAR-10, CelebA, ImageNet, and CelebA-HQ data and retain the same generation, memorization, and numerical-verification scenarios.

E2.justification: The VE-SDE conditioning baseline and the same unconditioning and temperature variants participate in the corresponding comparisons. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, sample counts, training budgets, preprocessing, model configurations, and sampling settings in Section 5 and Appendix B are identical.

E4.justification: The Cat-Caracal ablations, temperature and K sensitivity studies, pixel-versus-feature KNN comparisons, collapse-time analyses, and score/Jacobian investigations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including PyTorch seed 42 in Appendix B.1 and standard-deviation error bars across Gaussian shells in Figure 9. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and generated-image examples are identical. For example, Table 1 retains CIFAR-10 SDE (PC), 1K NFE training-set FIDs of 6.49 for conditioning and 7.33 for unconditioning; appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, propositions, derivations, and proofs are unchanged, including Appendix A's Gaussian-shell, score-domination, expansiveness, score-matching, and sampler analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about memorization, implicit neural-network smoothing, and the two proposed methods. The revised title does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including oversmoothing, memorization-metric limitations on CIFAR-10, qualitative-only large-scale evaluations, and unresolved questions about neural-network implicit bias in Appendix C.

D1.justification: Architecture, optimizer, hyperparameters, hardware, training-cost details, and data-processing instructions are unchanged. The code/model availability statement and embedded repository link also remain the same.

R1.justification: The cited works and discussions of prior research are identical. Removing the optimization-framework subtitle does not alter the retained optimization-based positioning in the paper.

P1.justification: The title is shortened and rephrased, removing 'An Optimization-based Explanation Framework.' The correspondence note changes from Stephen J. Wright to 'Equal Correspondence,' and the version/date stamp is updated. Section organization and scientific prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title changes from two lines to one, shifting first-page content and reflowing introductory text across pages 1–2. Figures, tables, and all layouts from page 3 onward are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The shorter title, correspondence update, and small layout adjustments do not materially change the paper's quality. Both versions contain identical scientific arguments, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations, with no substantive deficiency resolved or introduced.
